text: Later on 1 March 2008 the situation in Yerevan escalated and rallies continued throughout the city until the early morning of 2 March 2008.

text: On 2 March 2008 the applicant tried to enter Theatre Square in central Gyumri in order to hold a protest.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 2 March 2008 the applicant was refused entry to Theatre Square by police officers who were stationed there for the purpose of preventing any demonstrations from taking place.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: It is alleged that the applicant started calling on people who were present at Theatre Square to gather and to hold a demonstration.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: Police officers ordered the applicant to leave Theatre Square and to stop inciting others to assemble.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The applicant did not obey the police officers' orders to leave Theatre Square and to stop inciting others to assemble.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The applicant was taken to a police station after disobeying the police officers' orders at Theatre Square on 2 March 2008.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: At the police station an administrative case was initiated against the applicant under Article 182 of the Code of Administrative Offences for disobeying the lawful orders of the police officers.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: A record of an administrative offence was drawn up against the applicant at the police station.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: A statement was taken from the applicant at the police station.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The applicant was released from the police station after a record of an administrative offence was drawn up and a statement was taken from him.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 5 March 2008 the police lodged a claim with the Administrative Court seeking to subject the applicant to a penalty under Article 182 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The police stated in their claim that the applicant had called on others to hold a demonstration at Theatre Square in Gyumri.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The police stated in their claim that the applicant had refused to obey the lawful orders of the police officers, who had been stationed at Theatre Square for the purpose of preventing the conduct of unauthorised demonstrations, to stop his actions and to leave.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The police noted in their claim that the Gyumri Mayor's Office had not been duly notified of the demonstration at Theatre Square on 2 March 2008.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The police noted in their claim that no authorisation had been obtained to hold the demonstration at Theatre Square on 2 March 2008.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 24 March 2008 the applicant lodged a counter-claim against the police.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: In his counter-claim, the applicant argued that the police had failed to substantiate the factual basis of their claim, namely the fact that he had called on others to hold a rally.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: In his counter-claim, the applicant insisted that he had not intended to organise a rally and that there had not been any rally at Theatre Square at the material time.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: In his counter-claim, the applicant argued that the act of calling on people was not an act prohibited and therefore punishable by law.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: In his counter-claim, the applicant argued that no evidence had been produced to show that more than 100 people had gathered at or in the vicinity of Theatre Square at the material time.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: In his counter-claim, the applicant argued that the allegation that he had called on others to hold a rally without prior notification was unsubstantiated, since the law did not require prior notification if fewer than 100 people took part in a rally.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: In his counter-claim, the applicant argued that the police orders addressed to him could not be considered lawful.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On an unspecified date the police lodged a written response to the applicant's counter-claim, seeking to dismiss it as unsubstantiated.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The police claimed in their written response that well-known facts were not liable to be proved.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The police asserted that well-known facts included the fact that a tense situation had been created in Armenia after the tragic events of 1 March 2008, which threatened national security and public safety.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The police asserted in their written response that the day before the incident on 2 March 2008, an unauthorised rally had been held on Theatre Square in Gyumri, at which the time and place of the next rally had been announced.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The police asserted in their written response that at the unauthorised rally held the day before the incident, it had been announced that the applicant, who was known to be an active rally participant, would make a speech at Theatre Square.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The police asserted in their written response that it was not by chance that the applicant had appeared at Theatre Square on 2 March 2008, as he was not just an accidental passer-by.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The police asserted in their written response that the administrative case against the applicant was therefore justified.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 31 March 2008 the applicant lodged his objections to the police's written response, contesting the factual allegations made by the police.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 10 June 2008 the Administrative Court granted the police claim against the applicant.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 10 June 2008 the Administrative Court dismissed the applicant's counter-claim against the police.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 10 June 2008 the Administrative Court subjected the applicant to an administrative fine under Article 182 of the Code of Administrative Offences in the amount of 50,000 Armenian Drams (approximately 110 euros at the material time) for disobeying the lawful orders of the police officers.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Administrative Court held that on 2 March 2008 at around 12 noon police officers of the Gyumri Police Station were performing their duties at Gyumri's Theatre Square and its surroundings for the purpose of prohibiting the conduct of a demonstration in respect of which no notification had been made in accordance with the procedure prescribed by law.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Administrative Court found, referring to the requirements of Section 10 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, that there had been no legal basis for holding a demonstration at Theatre Square in Gyumri on 2 March 2008.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Administrative Court found that on 2 March 2008 at around 12.30 p.m. the applicant arrived at Theatre Square in Gyumri and wanted to enter the square, but was prevented and ordered to leave that area and not to call on people to gather and hold an event, which he disobeyed.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Administrative Court made reference to Sections 2, 12, 22 and 38 of the Police Act (2001).
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Administrative Court held that mass public events may be held only after notification in writing to the competent authority, in this case the Head of the Gyumri Community, in accordance with the requirements of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Administrative Court held that no notification of a mass public event on 2 March 2008 had been submitted to the Head of the Gyumri Community.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Administrative Court noted that the President of Armenia, by Decree no. NH-35-N of 1 March 2008, declared a state of emergency in Yerevan starting from 1 March 2008 for a period of twenty days for the purpose of preventing the threat to the constitutional order of the country and protecting the rights and lawful interests of the population.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Administrative Court found that the conduct of a mass public event in Gyumri, the second largest city of the country, could have endangered the protection of public order and public health, particularly when no notification to hold such an event had been submitted in accordance with the prescribed procedure.
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Administrative Court found that the police applied certain restrictions on gathering and holding events on Gyumri's Theatre Square pursuant to Article 43 of the Constitution of Armenia and the Police Act (2001).
section_path: II. THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Administrative Court concluded that the orders given to the applicant, which he had disobeyed, had been lawful.
